title: Income v capital — profit-making schemes (Myer, s 25A ITAA 1936, s 15-15 ITAA 1997)
summary: Facet map: is a profit on sale income or capital? Spine: date/regime (s 25A(1A) pre-20/9/1985 only; s 25A(1B) pre-1997-98 only — else s 15-15/Myer/CGT) → profit-making purpose at acquisition → Myer three conditions (purpose, commercial dealing, not mere realisation — Myer Emporium (1987) 163 CLR 199) → mere realisation boundary (Scottish Australian Mining (1950), Whitfords Beach (1982)) → income (s 6-5 or s 15-15) or capital (CGT) → legacy s 25A deeming cascade (ss 25A(2)-(10)) with the s 25A(3) Commissioner discretion. FACETS: Myer conditions detail, mere realisation doctrine, s 15-15 statutory limb, the s 25A(2)-(10) deeming cascade, s 25A(3) discretion, timing/derivation. Subsection coverage: s 25A(1), (1A), (1B), (2)-(10) all mapped; s 15-15(1)-(3) mapped. Rulings: TR 92/3, TR 1995/33.

nodes.label: You sell property and realise a profit — income or capital?
nodes.body: The single question with the most facets in Australian tax. Spine: date/regime → profit-making purpose → Myer scheme → mere realisation boundary → statutory/legacy limbs. Facets carry the case-law signposts and deeming machinery.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: When was the property acquired, and in which year did the profit arise?
nodes.body: s 25A(1A): NOT for property acquired on/after 20 September 1985. s 25A(1B): NOT for profits arising 1997-98+ from a profit-making undertaking/scheme (s 15-15 ITAA 1997 replaces it). Post-CGT, post-1997: the analysis is ordinary income (Myer) / s 15-15 / CGT.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: Apply the modern framework: Myer (s 6-5) + s 15-15 + CGT
nodes.body: For post-20/9/1985 property with 1997-98+ profits: s 6-5 ordinary income (Myer principle), s 15-15 statutory income (profit-making undertakings/plans), CGT Part 3-1 for capital gains.

nodes.label: Apply s 25A directly (pre-1985 property or pre-1997-98 profit)
nodes.body: s 25A(1): profit from (a) sale of property acquired for profit-making by sale, or (b) a profit-making undertaking or scheme. Deeming rules in ss 25A(2)-(10) extend this.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: Was the property acquired for the purpose of profit-making by sale?
nodes.body: The gateway for s 25A(1)(a) and s 15-15. Purpose must exist at acquisition and be the dominant/prevailing purpose, evidenced objectively. TR 1995/33 discusses subjective purpose.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

rulings.title: relevance of subjective purpose, motive or intention

nodes.label: Did you carry on a profit-making undertaking or scheme (Myer Emporium)?
nodes.body: Myer Emporium Ltd v FCT (1987) 163 CLR 199: profit on an isolated transaction is ordinary income where (1) purpose of profit-making at entry, (2) the transaction is a commercial dealing, (3) the profit is not a mere realisation of a capital asset. Operates through s 6-5.

statute.title: Income according to ordinary concepts (ordinary income)

cases.note: Myer Emporium Ltd v FCT (1987) 163 CLR 199

nodes.label: Was there an undertaking or scheme (a commercial operation), not a mere realisation?
nodes.body: Mere realisation of a capital asset is NOT income (Scottish Australian Mining (1950); FCT v Whitfords Beach (1982)). An organised commercial operation with profit purpose IS income. The line: extent of activity — subdivision, development, marketing, organised selling.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: Mere realisation — capital, not income
nodes.body: Capital gain under CGT (Part 3-1) for post-CGT assets; not assessable for pre-CGT assets. Scottish Australian Mining (1950), Whitfords Beach (1982).

nodes.label: Assessable as ordinary income (Myer) or statutory income (s 15-15)
nodes.body: Profit from a profit-making scheme is assessable: s 6-5 ordinary income (Myer) or s 15-15 statutory income. s 15-15(3): included in the year derived.

nodes.label: Do the s 25A(2)-(10) deeming rules apply (shares/interests in entities holding profit-making property)?
nodes.body: s 25A(2): selling shares in a private company, partnership interest, or private trust interest is deemed a sale of property acquired for profit-making by sale IF the entity held profit-making property (or through interposed entities). s 25A(3): Commissioner discretion NOT to apply. ss 25A(4)-(8): bonus shares, rights, transfers, mergers. ss 25A(9)-(10): Commissioner determines the profit.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: Deemed profit-making purpose — profit assessable under s 25A
nodes.body: Property deemed acquired for profit-making by sale; profit (Commissioner-determined under s 25A(9)) included under s 25A(1).

nodes.label: No deeming — capital (CGT) or not assessable
nodes.body: Post-CGT asset: capital gain subject to CGT (50% discount for individuals/trusts where applicable). Pre-CGT asset: not assessable.

nodes.label: Analysis complete
nodes.body: Profit is: (1) ordinary income (Myer, s 6-5); (2) statutory income (s 15-15); (3) assessable under s 25A (legacy); or (4) capital (CGT) / not assessable. Signposts: purpose at acquisition, commercial operation vs mere realisation, deeming provisions. TR 92/3 is the ATO's key guidance.

nodes.label: FACET — The Myer three conditions and their application
nodes.body: Where to look: Myer Emporium Ltd v FCT (1987) 163 CLR 199; TR 92/3; CCH 'isolated-transactions-myer-principle'. The three conditions: (1) purpose of profit-making at the time of entering the transaction (not merely at sale); (2) the transaction is a business operation or commercial transaction; (3) the profit is not a mere realisation of a capital asset. The principle applies to losses as well as profits (a Myer loss is deductible under s 8-1 if the transaction was a commercial dealing entered into for profit).

statute.title: Income according to ordinary concepts (ordinary income)

cases.note: Myer Emporium Ltd v FCT (1987) 163 CLR 199

nodes.label: FACET — The mere realisation doctrine and its limits
nodes.body: Where to look: Scottish Australian Mining Co Ltd v FCT (1950) 81 CLR 188 (subdividing and selling a mining property remained realisation); FCT v Whitfords Beach Pty Ltd (1982) 150 CLR 355 (company formed to develop land — business, not mere realisation); Californian Copper Syndicate v Harris (1904) (classic statement). The doctrine: profits from mere realisation, even with effort to enhance saleability, are capital unless the taxpayer is carrying on a business of selling or entered a profit-making scheme.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

cases.note: Scottish Australian Mining Co Ltd v FCT (1950) 81 CLR 188
FCT v Whitfords Beach Pty Ltd (1982) 150 CLR 355

nodes.label: FACET — s 15-15 ITAA 1997 (the statutory limb)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 15-15 (profit-making undertaking or plan — statutory income); s 15-15(2) (timing — profit derived when the undertaking/plan is carried out, subject to s 15-15(3)); s 15-15(3) (the profit is included in the year it is derived). s 25A(1B) diverts post-1997-98 profits to s 15-15.

nodes.label: FACET — The s 25A(2)-(10) deeming cascade in detail
nodes.body: Where to look: s 25A(2) (private company shares / partnership interests / private trust interests deemed profit-making where the entity holds profit-making property — sub-para (b)(i) direct, (b)(ii) through interposed entities); s 25A(3) (Commissioner's discretion having regard to assets, control, other sales); s 25A(4) (bonus shares and rights); s 25A(5) (prescribed transfers); s 25A(6)-(8) (merged interests, underlying property, transferred property); s 25A(9)-(10) (Commissioner determines the profit amount, with the pre-1985 adjustment).

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: FACET — The s 25A(3) Commissioner discretion
nodes.body: Where to look: s 25A(3) — the Commissioner may decide s 25A(2) should NOT apply, considering: (a) the extent to which the entity's assets consisted of the profit-making property immediately before sale; (b) the nature and extent of the taxpayer's control of the entity; (c) circumstances of other sales of interests in the entity; (d) such other matters as the Commissioner considers relevant. A protective discretion — the taxpayer can request it not be applied.

statute.title: Assessable income to include certain profits

nodes.label: FACET — Timing and year of derivation
nodes.body: Where to look: s 15-15(2)-(3) (profit derived when the undertaking/plan is carried out, in the year derived); s 25A(9) (Commissioner determines the profit and implicitly the year). CGT timing: CGT event A1 at disposal (contract date, s 104-10(3)). The income/capital character must be determined as at acquisition.
